utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters; good morning to the staff of the registry, the Defence counsel, the Prosecution. As you can see, we will be sitting with two Judges, only two of us. I wanted to inform the parties: Judge Wald has another case to sit in on, so unfortunately she is otherwise engaged in the services of the Tribunal. We were not able to modify the calendar. As you know, we have a very heavy schedule. I'm sure you will understand, and within the frameworks of Rule 15 bis, we will sit in this way today. We have one more witness for today. We're going to finish the witness today and won't leave him for next week. So if necessary, we shall even go on a little bit longer today, but I should like to appeal to the parties to make full use of our time, and I hope we'll be able to end by the end of the working day without having to prolong the sitting. I think that, having said that, Mr. Deretic, we can now call the witness, can we? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. We fully agree with what you have just said and we should like to take advantage of the occasion to say that we're going to call the last witness on our list, and that witness will be Witness DD/6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, will you please have the witness shown in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DD/6. Can you hear me? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Try to get yourself comfortable. Please approach the microphone. You're now going to take a look at what is written on the piece of paper to see if it is your name, and give us a yes or no answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Thank you for coming, Witness DD/6. We're going to refer to you in that way because that is your protective measure. You will now be answering questions put to you by Mr. Deretic. Mr. Deretic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you give us your full name and -- no, I apologise. Could you give us your full name and surname? No. I apologise once again. I seem to have got it wrong. This is a protected witness, so may we move into private session for a moment. And thank you to my learned colleagues for cautioning me of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, may I just inquire: A protected witness, but public, is that correct, in the sense of open testimony? Will the blinds be ... Thank you. Excuse me for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Quite so. I will ask the usher to raise the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, do you know Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I've known him for approximately 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know, prior to the war in Prijedor and the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, what he did and where Zoran Zigic was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, there has been a reference made to the "former Bosnia-Herzegovina." I'd like to correct the record. There is indeed a current Bosnia-Herzegovina which is a member state of the United Nations, and I would ask that that reference be stricken or corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I clarify? When it was the socialist republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, before the war. That's what I was referring to, and by the date and agreement, a new state was established which internationally recognised and which is now called the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: With that clarification, I think it's acceptable, but that was not what was said in the record, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that is what I understood from the beginning. I don't think we ought to turn the courtroom into a forum for political debate, and that's what I understood: Bosnia-Herzegovina before the conflict, which means a republic of the ex-Yugoslavia. That's how I understood it, but thank you for clarifying matters. I don't think, however, that we ought to turn this courtroom into something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was not the intention, it was just to make sure that there was a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, after the war broke out, were you engaged in the army of Republika Srpska on the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina; and if so, since when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I was in the police force. I was the reserve police force straight away, as soon as the takeover of power had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the Serbs took over power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: On the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether during this power takeover there were any armed conflicts in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the attack on Prijedor took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, do you happen to know, in view of the fact that you stated something a moment ago, that from the takeover of power in Prijedor you were in the reserve police force, that is to say, after the takeover of power until the attack on Prijedor, were there any armed conflicts in the Prijedor municipality area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know which was the first armed excess during that time frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: One of my colleagues was killed in front of the Bijelo Dugme from -- he was shot in the back for no reason at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you say colleague, do you mean a friend of yours, or do you mean a colleague because you were both policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. We were both policemen, or militiamen, as we used to call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And what was the Bijelo Dugme you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It's a cafe, a cafe bar, by the traffic lights, at a crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that cafe in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did that event take place in front of the cafe or in the cafe itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: In front of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that policeman who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I know his surname. It was Dzapa. I can't remember his name, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who killed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I just know the man's surname. He was a Muslim and his surname was Ceric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know, after the attack on Prijedor, whether, on the territory of Prijedor municipality, investigation centres were set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you enumerate those centres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I can. They were Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you personally have anything to do with any of those investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What was that? What were your links?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I was a guard in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when you arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Between the 10th and 15th of June, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who assigned you to that post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The commander who had been my commander up until then, Zivko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please: What year did you arrive in Keraterm? You said the 15th of June, but what year was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you arrived at Keraterm, and you said you went there to be a guard, where was your guard post, actually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: My guard post was at the entrance to Keraterm, that is to say, the gate, by the gates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, I should like us -- I should like the usher to show -- to place a copy of this photograph of Keraterm on the ELMO. And it is the only copy we have, I'm afraid, but I should like to ask the witness some questions concerning this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, does this photograph correspond to the Keraterm compound and the premises there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I can't see anything indicated on this photograph. You said "indicated."

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you see some facilities and features?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, yes, but it's difficult to find my way about it, because it's taken from above. The photograph is taken from above.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the picture on the ELMO. Now, does this photograph indicate the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, mostly, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On this picture, do you see the Prijedor-Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I apologise for interrupting, but we need a number for identifying this photograph. Ms. Krystal, could you give us a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be D9/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, you have the number, so if you mention the document again, would you please give us the number. That facilitates our work. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you indicate on the photograph, with respect to the road you have already pointed out, the direction of Prijedor and the direction of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Prijedor is here and Banja Luka is down here. It's a long way away, but it's in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should now like to ask the usher, with your permission, to provide the witness with a marker pen for the witness to be able to indicate certain positions on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you put a "PD" on the Prijedor direction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And then the Banja Luka direction, would you put "BL" for that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness DD/6, on this picture, could you show us where the entrance into the investigation centre of Keraterm was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And could you put a "U" for ulaz, entrance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now indicate where your guard post was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was there anything in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. There was a small hut or a kiosk. It was rather a large one, but that was where our guard post was, by that hut.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you place a "K" by the hut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, can you tell us, as a guard, what were your duties in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, we had a number of duties, but my main duties was to prevent civilians to come to the detainees, that is to say, the people being investigated. My second task was to lock and unlock the dormitories; and the third duty which we did on occasion was to take individuals for interrogation to the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Among other things, was it one of your duties to see to the distribution of food to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who the people were who were detained in this investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Mostly Muslims and Croats who were brought there to be interrogated, whether they had taken part in the attack, whether they had done anything against the authorities, and in fact, to ascertain things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: The people that were brought to Keraterm, were they interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where did that questioning take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: In the premises on the first floor of Keraterm. I don't know how to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you show us on the ELMO, on the picture there, where those premises were located exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, you can't see it exactly, but the entrance was here. They would go upstairs, and the rooms were over here. I can't quite see because you see the roof on the picture, so I can't see behind the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When these detainees were interrogated, did anybody escort them to the interrogation room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes; always a guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you one of the guards who escorted the detainees when they went for questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who interrogated those individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: They were inspectors but people I didn't know, so I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I heard that they were from Prijedor and from Banja Luka, but that's what people said. I can't say for sure myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the detainees after they were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Do you want me to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was: We would bring the prisoner upstairs. We got a list, and we would bring the detainees on that list, first one, then the second, and then the third. We would bring them to the door, we would knock on the door, open the door for the detainees to go in, then we would close the door and wait outside. Then the detainee would come out, he would give us a list, a piece of paper to say where he was to be taken, whether Room 1 or 2. First of all, it was 1 and 2, and then there were Rooms 1, 2, 3, and 4, but you were told on this piece of paper where to take the detainee to afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After the interrogations, do you know whether any of the individuals were released, were allowed to go home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that you came to Keraterm between the 10th and 15th of June, 1992, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Keraterm, did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The first day, straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see him after that, during the following days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I saw him once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, could you tell us what Zoran Zigic did in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: He drove a minivan and he brought water and food. That was his job there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where was that water and food taken from to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I assume that it was brought from the barracks, but I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zoran was ever assisted by any of the detainees when he would bring water and food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that. Perhaps only when he was taking things out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you see Zoran Zigic for the first time, and when did you see him after that; that is, when you would see him, do you remember how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He always wore the same kind of clothes, so I can easily remember. He always had a camouflage uniform on and a red beret on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you would see him, when you saw him, was there anything characteristic about him as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. He had a bandage on his left arm -- on his left hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Zoran was armed on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It depended. Sometimes he was, sometimes he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What kind of weapon did Zoran have when he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I think he had a pistol, probably a Scorpion, but it was a handgun, a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you came to Keraterm and after you saw Zoran there, did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During those conversations, did Zoran tell you anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that his hand hurt when he cleaned his weapon, that he had problems using his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know why he had a bandage on his hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I was told that, in a shooting incident, he lost his forefinger, his index finger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During those several days when you saw Zigic, did you ever see him riding a motorcycle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you saw him, when you saw Zoran Zigic, how did he behave on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: You would first hear him and then see him, because he always made a lot of noise. I would first actually hear him and then saw him. It was always the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who did he talk to within the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Everybody. He had a lot of friends amongst the police and the military, and the detainees as well, so he talked to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, when you used to see him, did you ever happen to see him beat anyone in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During those days, did you ever see Zoran Zigic come to Keraterm during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When were you on duty? Only during the day or during the night, or both during the day and during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It depended. I would first be on duty for 12 hours during the day, and then the next day for 12 hours during the night. That's how it happened. Those were the shifts. And then we would be 24 hours off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the testimony, you indicated that when you arrived in Keraterm, you saw Zoran on that particular day, on two or three other occasions. Did that happen during the following two or three days or did you see him two or three times on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but I think it was on that first -- on those first two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After that, did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, do you know the person by the name of Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Emsud Bahonjic, was he brought to the camp before or after your arrival in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When I came to Keraterm, he was already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where was he put up? In which room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Room 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: At the time of your arrival in Keraterm, how many rooms were used to accommodate detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were they marked with numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, they were; Room 1 and Room 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and indicate to us on the photograph where those two rooms were located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Here is the Room 1, and then Room 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark them with numbers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you stated that later on some additional rooms were used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. Number 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably after the attack on Prijedor, after what happened in Kozarac, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate on the photograph where Rooms number 3 and 4 were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Emsud Bahonjic had a nickname while he was in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I didn't have many contacts with him. I knew him, Emsud Bahonjic, but I know that he was arrested when he carried a rifle called Singapurka, and that's why they called him Singapurac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you meet Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Immediately after my arrival, a day or two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Since we cannot see your answer on the record, let me repeat the question: When did you learn about his nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Only after the events in Keraterm, after everything was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How did you meet Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When I arrived in Keraterm during those first days, a Muslim came, and he said that he was ill, that somebody was ill. And I went to see what it was all about and I saw him holding his stomach, and he was taken to hospital on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when that happened in relation to your arrival in Keraterm? Was that on the same day or later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: During those first three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long Emsud stayed in hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: He left while I was on duty, while my shift was on duty, and then when I arrived to do my night shift, I found him there again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When he was taken to hospital, do you know what time it was? Was that during the day or the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was sometime between 11.00 and 12.00, around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Emsud Bahonjic was beaten in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he beaten before he was taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When he came back from hospital, he was called out on a daily basis. He was taken out every day and beaten up by whoever came from the outside. There were groups of people, including soldiers, and nothing could be done about it. It could not have been prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How long did it last; one day, several days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Two or three days. Three days, I believe. I think that he was found dead on the third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic in Keraterm during those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I know that he tried to escape and that he was found in the pallets between the military police facility and Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, could you show us where those pallets were situated? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The pallets were here. That is where the military police was. That was their main building. This is where they had a guard post, and those pallets were stacked one on top of the other here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: So the pallets were placed in the shape of letter "A", like this, and he was found there, near those pallets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark them with letter "P", "P" and "L", please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: "PL" for pallet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: This whole row here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: At what part of the day this incident took place? When was he found on the pallet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: As I was locking up the dormitory in the evening, half past 9 or 10.00, it was my duty to lock the dormitories. I went to dormitory number one, and the person who was in charge of Room 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The person who was in charge of that room told me that one detainee was missing. So I locked up all the dormitories and informed the duty officer about his absence, and the duty officer informed the commander of the investigation centre about that, and later on, we were told to search the premises of the centre. Since the TO was already there - they were the ones who provided security during the night - it was their task to search the premises, and we were told to remain on our guard posts and watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you mean by "TO"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of the Prijedor town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was it a special unit which was located in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was a unit which consisted mainly of elderly people who were not able to go to the front line, of 50 years old and more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you as a guard take part in that search for Emsud Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After he was found near the pallets, Emsud Bahonjic, what happened afterwards? What happened with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When I realised it was him, I went back to my guard post, and the members of the territorial guard remained there and started beating him up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you actually see the members of the TO beating Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I saw them when they hit the first time, and then I turned around. I couldn't, I couldn't watch it. This is something I cannot watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Why as a guard you did not intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I could have lied down next to him. That was the only thing I could have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you have authority, were you able to prevent any such misconduct of the members of the Territorial Defence within the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: We had authority during the day; however, during the night, they were in charge of security. I already explained to you what our task was. We had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When they came back, the members of the Territorial Defence, they passed by the fence where I was standing. I heard them saying, "This one is finished," something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Later on, did you, did you go over to that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Until what time were you on duty that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It lasted until 6 or 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you know at that point in time what had happened with Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No. It was only later on that I heard that he had died.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, do you know an individual by the name of Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How do you know Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When I arrived in Keraterm, I found him there, and I was told that he was a dangerous individual and that I should not go near him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you arrived in Keraterm, was Drago Tokmadzic already there, or was he brought there after you arrived in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No. I found him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: He wore a police uniform with a red star on his cap. It was the old kind of police uniform that we used to have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where, in which room Drago Tokmadzic was placed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Room 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know why he was put there in that particular room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Probably because less severe cases were taken in Room 1, that is, the individuals who were not considered to be guilty of anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did Drago Tokmadzic stay in Room 2 throughout that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While you were on duty, do you know whether Drago Tokmadzic was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: He was beaten every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he was beaten during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Both during the day and night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the reasons why Drago Tokmadzic was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: He had been an active policeman prior to the war, and he had had conflicts with a number of people. Everybody said that he had been a very violent and aggressive policeman, that he would beat people up, and that's why people wanted to avenge themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who beat Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Various groups of people: members of the military, police, the reserve police, people who would come from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you watch when Drago Tokmadzic was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No. No. I wouldn't. I would just see the beginning of the beating incident and I would go back to my guard post.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you please come closer to the microphone. I cannot hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Anyway, I would not watch those beatings. I would move away, because I was sorry. I felt sorry for everybody. That's the kind of person I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, did you see Zoran Zigic beat Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic amongst the soldiers who were beating Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I never saw him with those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what happened with Drago Tokmadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I heard that he did not survive the beating, that one morning he was found dead. But I was not on duty at that time, so I don't know for sure, but this is at least what I heard from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: From my colleagues. There were rumours, stories. People talked to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: This happened a long time ago, I know, but could you perhaps remember when Drago Tokmadzic died as a result of those beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Perhaps seven days after my arrival in Keraterm, but I really cannot be sure. It was a long time ago. But it must have been seven or eight days after my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zoran Zigic kill anyone in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No. I am a hundred per cent sure I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an incident in Keraterm when a number of people were killed during one night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was during the night between the 24th and 25th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you on duty? Was your shift on duty at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What shift was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was the night shift, in the night between the 24th to the 25th, from 7.00 in the evening to 7.00 in the morning, or from 6.00 to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive to take up your shift that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I came between 6.00 and 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you repeat when your -- how long did your night shift last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was a long time ago. It was either from 7.00 to 7.00 or from 6.00 to 6.00, so this difference -- I give you this difference now because I can't remember whether it was from 6.00 in the evening to 6.00 in the morning or from 7.00 in the evening to 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, Witness DD/6, in more precise terms, from 1800 to 1900 hours in the evening and then until 6.00 a.m. or 7.00 a.m. in the morning? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the day was like? I'm talking about the day, the weather. What was the weather like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was hot. It was about 30 degrees centigrade. It was very hot, and that is a time of year when it is generally hot in our country. So that's what the weather was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you take over your shift, and were you at the same guard post that evening as you described earlier, the guard post you always did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you came to take up your shift, did you notice anything out of the ordinary compared to the previous days or nights when you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything out of the ordinary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And would you please, Witness, make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I can't hear the interpretation very well, so I don't know when it overlaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could the usher put the volume up for the witness in his headsets, because it appears that the witness can't hear the interpretation very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Is that better, Witness? Can you hear me now? Can you hear me properly now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you, but I can't hear their interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Well, anyway, please try and make pauses between my question and your answers. Thank you. Let me repeat my last question again. After you took over your shift, did you notice anything out of the ordinary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: When I arrived, everything seemed normal. I would go up to them, I would see everything was in order. Most of them were outside, in front of the rooms. Nothing out of the ordinary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether on that particular evening the Keraterm compound was lit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was always lit. It was lighted up all the time. There were lights around here, by the fence. They were the big kind of lights with the pillars, the lampposts, sort of round lampposts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were all the lights working, burning, that night, that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many lights were actually working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Two to three.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you see the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How long were you in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Up until about the end of July. I left thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you about that particular evening. How long were you in Keraterm that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: About 9.00, 9.30 p.m., and then I left. Do you want me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before you left your shift, did you make a tour of the rooms and lock them up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of Rooms 1, 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you made the tour of the rooms to lock them up, did you notice anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how you locked Room 1; with what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: There was a lock and chain on Room 1, and I think on Room 4, whereas Rooms 2 and 3 had an ordinary lock with a key, not the chain-and-lock system.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: That evening, before you left, did you receive any reinforcements, any people come as reinforcements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: We would get reinforcements all the time. There were not enough guards and a large number of detainees, so the TO, members of the Territorial Defence of the town of Prijedor, would come as reinforcements to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When would they arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: About 9, 9.30, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How would they come to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: They would come by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, was the Keraterm compound secured by weapons, arms? Were they used to guard it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Since when were those weapons positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Since the very beginning they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What was the security for Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: We had the infantry rifles of the men and machine-guns as well, two machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where the machine-guns were positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate that to us on this picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was to the left, hereabouts. There was a barrier here, and that's where the first one was, and the other one was more to the right, over here. That was where the barrier, sandbag barrier was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you put "number 1" in the position where the first machine-gun was. Put "M1," please, Witness, "M1" for the first machine-gun, and "M2" to denote the second machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you happen to remember whether at that time in the Keraterm compound there was a weighing-in device of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What kind of weighing-in device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, to measure the weight of the trucks, the load, the freight of the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was there a hut next to this weighing-in device or scales?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you locate that hut on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes. This is the hut, and this is where the weighing-in machine was. It was rather a big one so that the truck could actually go onto it, onto the device, and be weighed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you mark that in for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Like this, this is what it looked like. The truck would move up onto that weighing device.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And what about the hut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The hut was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could we put a "V" for vaga or weighing-in device.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: This is it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/6, you said that you left the Keraterm compound that evening. Could you tell us what time again, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Between 9 and 9.30 p.m., or 2100 hours, 2130 hours, whichever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Because I had some private business to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what it was about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, if you think it's essential, but I don't think it's anything important. They were my own private affairs, some private business that I had to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you leave Keraterm with or without permission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I asked the duty officer, and he gave me permission; that is to say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you were going out of Keraterm, was -- when you were leaving Keraterm, was everything "normal"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you return that night to the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you come back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Between 4 and 5 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you entered the Keraterm compound, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The compound was lit up. There was some sporadic gunshots, and we had to -- can I indicate this on the picture, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead. That would be a good idea.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: There was shooting, sporadic gunfire that is, and we had to move through -- past the military police and go along the fence to enter Keraterm 'cause we were -- because we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you entered the Keraterm compound, was the situation the same as when you left the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No. Do you wish me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: The compound was lit up more. There was shooting, there was a great deal of commotion, a lot of people, and the compound looked quite different. It was no longer the compound -- the kind of compound I left. It looked -- everything looked different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, they were all scattered this way. Some of them had been fleeing this way and were lying there, and other people were lying along this wall here. I could see them very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that better? Is that all right? I'm not getting the interpretation either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should be on channel 6, on channel 6. I'm getting the English interpretation. May we try again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps you have changed channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation] I see that the English court reporter can't hear now, so there seems to be a problem. Witness, can you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear the French booth myself. [In English] I'm hearing the English booth, too, so ... What about the English court reporter, can you hear? Mr. Deretic, please proceed and we'll see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you returned to the Keraterm compound, was the compound lit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, it was more strongly lit when I came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How were you able to notice this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I saw that there were some strong lights beamed towards Room 3. Do you want me to explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where was the light coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: From a reflector light that had probably been set up that night, because when I left, it wasn't there; when I came back, I saw this reflector light had been put into position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on the picture where that reflector light was, and could you place an "R" for the reflector light.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was on a post, set up on a post, and that was the first time that I saw a reflector light of that kind. It was enormous, a very big one. A searchlight, in fact. It was a big searchlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything else beside the searchlight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did. A row of people, mostly soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Which soldiers were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, they were the territorial units, the intervention platoon from Prijedor I Police Station, but at least I didn't know them. Most of them were people I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did any of them shoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many dead bodies you saw in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: In the compound. You mean in front of the rooms, the dormitories?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Will you explain to us if you saw them and where you saw them and how many you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, it will be best for me to explain to you like this: There were five or six dead bodies in front of these doors; three of them were piled up, one on top of the other, in front of this door; and over here there were another three or four. That's what I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that you stayed there until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you leave your shift at 6.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: That night, were a number of people killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people were killed that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to say with any certainty, but what I heard that they had loaded - and it was about an hour - I would say about 50 people at the most, about 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before you left your shift, before you went off duty, did you see a truck of any kind in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before you left, did you unlock the rooms where the detainees were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did you call anyone out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we go into private session for a few moments for my next question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. Deretic, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you returned in the morning, you said that you returned about between 3.00 and 4.00 a.m. Did you see Zoran Zigic then in the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you -- could you have seen Zoran Zigic amongst those soldiers who were there in the compound had he been there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, if he had been there, I must have seen him, I would have seen him, and if not seen him, I would have heard him; that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Why did you say "hear him, that's for sure"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, because he was always very loud. He would make a lot of noise. You could hear him two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you come on duty next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I was off for 24 hours and then I took up my shift after that 24-hour break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And how long were you in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Until the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During those wartime events, did you happen to see Zoran Zigic around the town of Prijedor at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform, the kind that you described and the cap you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I apologise for interrupting, but could you tell us how much more time you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, Mr. President. I am looking at my watch all the time, and I should like to get through this before the break. I will need five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said a moment ago that you have known Zoran for at least 25 years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you met him the first time, what was his hair colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you would meet, that is to say, during those war years, did you ever happen to notice Zoran dye his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he have earrings in his ears during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I never saw him with earrings, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he ever wear black gloves with the fingers cut off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I never saw that either, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During that time when you would see Zigic, Zoran Zigic, do you happen to know whether he drank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he drink moderately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No, not moderately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question. During that period of time, did Zigic, Zoran, drink moderately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, how can I say? He always drank too much, and whenever I saw him, he would always be drunk, practically always.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: These meetings of yours, where were they, generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, we would meet in cafes, in bars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you describe those meetings for us briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I would go into a bar. I went into this cafe called Trij Lipe to have a glass of something. Usually I drink Coca-Cola, but when I went in and saw Zigic sitting there, he noticed me and then I wasn't able to leave. I had to sit down with him. He asked me what I was going to drink, and he [as interpreted] said, "I'll have a juice." And he said, "No, you can't have a juice," and wouldn't let the waitress bring me a juice. I had to drink -- he said, "You can either have a beer or something stronger," and I had to obey. That's how it was. I had a bit more to drink. I had about three beers, and then I left. That was our meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he under the influence of alcohol then? Was he intoxicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this particular event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: It was sometime in the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And two more questions, Mr. President, if I may, with the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What was his behaviour in situations of that kind, Zoran Zigic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, you could never be certain whether he was going to hit you or be friendly towards you, so I would always approach him with a great deal of reserve. I was never quite certain what to expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And my final question for you, Witness: How would you describe Zoran Zigic as a person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, when he was sober, he was all right; when he had something to drink, it was better to steer clear of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DD/6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that completes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Deretic. Thank you. I think that this is -- that it's time for our break, but before we break, I should like to ask the usher to lower the blinds and escort the witness out of the courtroom. And I say for the purposes of the public gallery that this witness enjoys protective measures, so we're going to lower the blinds, and we have a half-hour break. A half-hour break. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Witness DD/6, you're now going to answer questions that will be put to you by the counsel for the Prosecution. Madam Susan Somers, you have the floor for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [redacted]would you please -- Sorry. Witness [redacted]would you please indicate your present occupation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I work in a private company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is the private company, name and location, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If it does not provide any identifying information as to your own identity, please indicate what you do for that company and for how long you have worked there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, I think I have already provided you with some identifying information by saying where I work. I think I will have to disclose my identity if I go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, we could perhaps move into private session. The witness will feel more comfortable when answering your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are, I think, in private [as interpreted] -- in public session already. Ms. Somers, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, public session. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You were explaining how you came to know Mr. Zigic, and you gave some indication that it was through your brother. And can you tell us, please: Over the years, indicate the frequency or the intervals, the intervals at which you saw and spent time with Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: With Zoran Zigic. I think you said "Goran Zigic," and we're talking about Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I meant Zoran. If you heard "Goran," I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I apologise too. At the beginning, I used to see him almost every day while he was a taxi driver, because I would come to see my brother and they would be together. After that, I saw him less frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when you say "less frequently," can you indicate, please: Did you see him once a week, once a day, once a month, once a year? And particularly, in 1992, 1993, emphasising that period, how frequently did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Before the war, at the beginning, almost every day, two or three days. After that, I would see him perhaps once a month, and then later on, perhaps only once a year. In 1992, during the war, I saw him at the beginning, when I came to Keraterm, and then in 1993 I saw him once again, and after that, I don't remember seeing him at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your arrival at Keraterm was substantially after the camp opened, was it not? The camp had been opened at least three weeks when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry to intervene because of some banal things and to have to interrupt the cross-examination, but I have to say that the question contains a conclusion, that is, that there was a period of time of three weeks between the opening of the camp and the arrival of the witness. I'm not a very good mathematician at all, but that would have been sometime around the 26th, and that is not what the witness - I'm sorry - sometime around the 20th of June, and that is not what the witness stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'll be happy to rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do so. I can see the word "substantially" in the record. That's perhaps not something that we should be using.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The Kozarac area was taken over, and we have used the term - perhaps you use a different term - "cleansed," on the 24th of May, 1992. Are you familiar with that particular occurrence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: As far as I know, it took place before that, before the 24th and the 25th, maybe three or four days prior to that, and we also use the term "cleanse."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The individuals who were taken from Kozarac, the non-Serbs, are you able to tell us whether or not you know if they were in Keraterm? Would you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Yes, of course I knew that. I was there, and when they arrived, they had to pass by me, where I stood.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. So then, Witness DD/6, persons from the Kozarac area who had been removed were in Keraterm, and are you familiar with the fact that there was an overflow of population and persons were then moved to Omarska? Just so we can get a time frame about when the camps may have opened. Perhaps that would assist you a little bit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I know that some went to Omarska, some were in Keraterm. Those were the two main groups of people, how they were distributed, mainly for reasons of space.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Then we can agree, just so it's clear, that when the incident at Kozarac occurred, those non-Serb persons were taken to Keraterm? If that's a fair statement, I would just ask you to let me know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: They were both in Keraterm and Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness was clear as to the time of his arrival in Keraterm, and he specified that people passed him by when he came. Up until now, he hasn't spoken about the events that took place prior to the opening of the Keraterm camp. My learned colleague is drawing conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the solemn declaration that was signed is a May declaration, the events that occurred after the takeover by the Serbs of this area are very relevant, and I think it is critical that we test the witness's knowledge of events and of his knowledge of who would or would not have been in Keraterm, at which camp he has admitted serving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, but my concern was the fact that the witness said after the takeover of Kozarac some of them were taken to Keraterm and some to Omarska. I mean, that is the fact that we have to bear in mind. Please continue with your questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: If I may be given the floor, please. The solemn declaration was signed only afterwards. We had already been with the police, and we had signed the declaration and photographs were taken. But it happened only after, sometime later. We were already with the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, the witness has indicated -- has answered sufficiently for my purposes, unless the Chamber has another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You have also mentioned that you worked various shifts or, at least, you staggered your hours. Tell us, please, the name of your shift leader at Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I could do that, but I think we would again have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would disagree, but if the Chamber feels this is essential, I think that it probably would not be a giveaway, but I would leave that in the Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is preferable to move into private session if the witness would feel more comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... role - I beg your pardon - of Sikirica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: His role was he would come by car, tour it, make a tour of it, that sort of thing. Let me explain how I got to know him, if you want to -- if you want me to. But once again, this would require us to go back into private session if you want me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I don't think that will be necessary. I'd like to ask you, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence of Mr. Zigic once again would like to refer to Rule 95 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and the subject of the cross-examination is not now linked to the examination-in-chief. This seems to be an investigation or interrogation about other persons, and we should like to object along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, do you see any difference here with respect to the discussion we had and the position we took yesterday with respect to an identical situation that cropped up then?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I consider, Mr. President, that there is a difference here with respect to the way in which the Prosecution asked the question. In the examination-in-chief of the witness, we did not mention the individual that was brought up now with respect to any of his functions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Susan Somers, is your response the same as it was yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the position of the Chamber -- the position of the Chamber remains unchanged. We assume the same position. These questions are relative to the indictment and relevant to the case. We have already said that there are different interpretations of that particular rule. The Chamber takes a broader view, a broader interpretation of the issue, but the Chamber also considers that certain discipline and organisation must be applied. I think that we decided that the clearest way to limit the Prosecutor -- the best way to limit the Prosecutor was time, the time factor. And as I said yesterday, if Ms. Susan Somers has questions to ask with respect to sport or someone from the cinema, I'll cut her off there at that point, but I'm not going to cut her off here. So please, Ms. Susan Somers, continue, but please bear in mind that I'm going to be very strict as to the time you take.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if you recall Zoran Zigic being present at -- sorry, at Keraterm when Dusan or Dusko Sikirica was at Keraterm? Do you recall that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask, please, excuse me, that Exhibit 3/249 be distributed. If the usher is also able to place the exhibit on the ELMO after distributing, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In front of you is a document dated 4th of July, 1992. It is a note, official note, which purports to bear the signature of Dusko Sikirica, and this note indicates that it was compiled on the 4th of July, in the offices of Prijedor II Wartime Police Station RSM, regarding Zoran, son of Nikola, Zigic, and it goes on to state that: "Zoran Zigic, an armed, uniformed person (I do not know which unit he belongs to) came to the Keraterm Reception Centre several times at night, together with Dusko Knezevic, Zoran Vokic, and Zeljko Timarac. "Despite our warnings not to enter the reception centre compound, they entered, explaining that they were going to talk to one of the prisoners. According to the guards, they beat prisoners to exhaustion, after which they left. Those beaten would die a few days after they left. "I hereby ask the responsible bodies to suggest to the military command that," and it's difficult to read this in English, "such conscripts should be prevented from committing these arbitrary acts. "Any intervention on our part would result in an armed conflict, which is not in anyone's interest at this moment." And it bears, or purports to bear, a signature of Dusko Sikirica. Now, this date, July 4th, from your testimony, was a date during which you were working; at least, that was during the time period, as I understood your testimony, where you in fact were working at Keraterm. Help me understand. You indicated that you had four responsibilities, four areas of responsibility: One was to prevent civilians from getting to the detainees; another was to lock and unlock the dormitories; another was to take individuals for interrogation; and then later you added distribution of food and water. Were you called in at any point by Sikirica or anyone in command of Keraterm about the entries referred to in this document of Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know an individual at Keraterm by the name of Dosen, first name Damir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know if Dosen used any other last name? Was he ever referred to by any other last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I don't know. I know him by his surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard him referred to as Petkovic, perhaps? Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an individual named Danka Petkovic? Did you ever know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I ever knew a woman by the name of Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you know any nicknames used by Dosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD/6
utterances.text: Well, let me explain. Dosen and I grew up together and I always knew him as Dosen, but I didn't know a nickname. That's an absurd question to ask me. I said that I knew him as Dosen, and that's how I knew him. We grew up together and I always knew him as Dosen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
